plainTranslation: A's mind meets B's dreams. The opposition pulls them into push-and-pull.

summaryDeep:
This person can feel like the conversation you have been waiting your whole life to have.

Something in you relaxes around them. They seem to grasp the hidden parts of your mind, the parts you usually have to explain too carefully to anyone else, and you find yourself speaking more openly, sharing thoughts that normally stay locked behind your teeth. The pull is not only mental. It is hypnotic. You want to keep talking because the conversation itself feels like a sanctuary you can live inside.

Because this is an opposition, you are standing across a divide, and you have to stay awake. The connection slips easily into projection. One of you may be doing more imagining than listening. You might hear depth in their silence because you need it to be there. You might hear agreement in their vagueness because agreement is what you are hoping for. They may be doing the same to you. You reflect each other, and the trouble lives in the blur: you cannot always tell whether you are seeing them or seeing your own longing handed back to you.

At its best, the two of you balance across the divide. One provides the anchor, giving language and definition to what was vague. The other provides the ocean, keeping the exchange from going dry, literal, or small. Between you, there is room for both soaring imagination and plain clarity.

The quiet damage is in how you dismiss each other. One of you asks for proof of something that cannot be proven and makes the other feel doubted. The other treats plain logic as too small, too literal, a failure to feel, and makes the first one feel shut out. Neither of you usually means to. Both of you end up feeling unseen in exactly the place you most wanted to be understood. The shadow takes over when you fall in love with the feeling of the conversation and stop asking whether it is true. You read between the lines until the lines disappear. You decide this person wants what you want, means what you mean, sees what you see. Then the fog clears, reality arrives, and the disappointment can be brutal. There is a particular pain in realizing you were partly talking to your own dream.

Keep returning to the shore. Come back to what was actually said, not what you hoped was meant.
